questions.question: Compare the Highveld and the Lowveld: where they are, what they are like and how people use them.
questions.expected_answer: The Highveld is high grassland on the plateau, in Gauteng, the Free State and parts of Mpumalanga and North West, with summer thunderstorms and cold, frosty winters; it is used for maize, sunflowers, wheat, cattle, cities and coal mines. The Lowveld is lower land below the escarpment in the east of Mpumalanga and Limpopo, hot with mild winters and bushveld; it has the Kruger National Park and tropical fruit farms.

questions.question: Explain the difference between the Great Karoo and the Little Karoo.
questions.expected_answer: The Great Karoo is a large, dry, mostly flat region on the southern plateau, between the Great Escarpment and the Swartberg, with Karoo bushes, sheep and goat farms and windmills. The Little Karoo is a long, narrow valley in the Western Cape between the Swartberg to the north and the Langeberg and Outeniqua mountains to the south, with irrigated farms and ostriches around Oudtshoorn.

questions.question: Describe the Kalahari and Namaqualand and say where each is.
questions.expected_answer: The Kalahari is a semi-desert of red sand with grass, bushes and camel thorn trees, in the north of the Northern Cape and into Botswana and Namibia. Namaqualand is in the far north-west along the Atlantic coast, dry and rocky, with winter rain and famous wild flowers in August and September.
